ulid.description: A ULID in Crockford base32 capitals: a Rakumux session id, the id the daemon gave a reply, or the id the cloud gave an attached file.

seq.description: The cloud's arrival order for one user's entries: increasing, never reused.

label.description: One visible line: no terminal, format, default-ignorable, surrogate or line/paragraph controls.

machine.description: The machine the reply was made on, as its owner names it (the host name).

session.description: The Rakumux session the reply was made in. `folder` is the folder's last path component only, never a path; `branch` is the git branch its agent worked on when the turn finished.

agent.description: The coding agent, by the name Rakumux gives it: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI (`copilot`), Cursor Agent CLI (`cursor-agent`), Pi, Grok, Kimi Code (`kimi`), Droid or Amp. A machine leaves out what another agent said.

replyText.description: What the agent said when it finished its turn, as plain text. Tab, LF and CR are allowed; other terminal controls, format controls, default-ignorables and lone surrogates are not.

upload.description: One finished reply as a machine uploads it.

truncated.description: The reply was longer and `text` is its start.

position.description: The position of the turn's last message in its chat (`chat-upload`), so the cloud can find the turn. Absent from older machines: the turn then ends at its chat's last message at or before `finished_at`.

reply_to.description: The feed reply (`reply`) this turn answers: the machine typed it into the session and this is the agent's next reply there.

position.description: Where a message is in its conversation; messages sort by it. A byte offset into the agent's log for Claude Code and Codex; for OpenCode, its own order times 1024 plus the block's index.

messageId.description: A message's id within its conversation: the agent's own (Claude Code's entry uuid, OpenCode's ids) or its position.

callId.description: The agent's id for a tool call, which its result names too.

subagentId.description: A subagent's id, unique in its chat: Claude Code's agent id, OpenCode's child session id, GitHub Copilot's agent id.

subagent.description: The subagent a message is from: an agent the chat's agent started with a tool call (Claude Code's `Agent`, OpenCode's and GitHub Copilot's `task`), working in a conversation of its own. A subagent's messages sort among themselves by `position` (its own log's) and belong under the call that started it (`call_id`, in the main conversation or in another subagent's), which has its result once the subagent ended. Any of its messages may leave out `call_id` and `label` once one gave them.

call_id.description: The tool call that started it.

label.description: What it was asked to do: its description, else its agent type.

partText.description: A message part's text as plain text, at most 64 KiB (longer text is cut and the part says `truncated`). Tab, LF and CR are allowed; other terminal controls, format controls, default-ignorables and lone surrogates are not.

partOutput.description: A tool call's input or a tool's output: `partText`, but it may be empty.

truncated.description: The text was longer and this is its start.

part.description: One piece of a message, by `type`: what was written (`text`), the agent's visible reasoning (`reasoning`), a tool call and its input (`tool_call`; `input` is usually JSON) or a tool's output (`tool_result`).

message.description: One message of a chat: one entry of the agent's conversation, or of one of its subagents' (`subagent`). `user` is what the user typed (or, in a subagent's, what it was asked), `assistant` the agent's text, reasoning and tool calls, `tool` tools' output. Uploading an id again replaces the message (OpenCode changes its messages as they stream).

at.description: When the agent wrote it, on the machine's clock.

subagent.description: The subagent whose conversation it is from; absent from the main conversation's messages (and from older machines'). Only to a cloud whose `sessions-stored` `accepts` has `subagents`.

chat.description: An agent's conversation on one machine, with the Rakumux session that last showed it.

promptText.description: What the user writes back to an agent, as plain text of at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes. Tab, LF and CR are allowed; other terminal controls, format controls, default-ignorables and lone surrogates are not.

fileName.description: An attached file's name as the user's browser gave it: one visible line of at most 128 characters and 255 UTF-8 bytes (what a file name may take on Linux and macOS), never a path (no `/` or `\`), `.` or `..`. Two files of one reply may share a name.

mediaType.description: An attached file's media type, `type/subtype` in lowercase without parameters: what the user's browser said, or `application/octet-stream` when it said nothing. Informational only: nobody checks it against the file, and the file is always downloaded as `application/octet-stream`.

attachment.description: A file the user attached to a reply on rakumux.com: its id (for `GET /api/v1/feed/replies/attachments/{id}`), name, media type and size.

size.description: The file's length in bytes, 1 to 4 MiB: what the download's body holds.

replyStatus.description: `pending` until the entry's machine types it into the session (`delivered`) or can't (`failed`); `expired` when it stayed pending an hour.

replyFailure.description: Why a reply wasn't delivered: the session isn't running on its machine (`session_gone`), shows another conversation now (`conversation_changed`), is private (`private`), the machine doesn't take replies from rakumux.com or other machines (`not_accepted`: only from older releases, while a setting of theirs is off), the session refused the text (`refused`), a file attached to it couldn't be fetched or wasn't what the reply said (`attachment_unavailable`), or it was typed in but its agent didn't take it as a prompt (`not_taken`: its chat showed no new prompt within 30 seconds, or another one; it may still be in the session's input box; for an answer, keys went into its dialog but it didn't take them as given, and it may be partly answered there), or an answer's question isn't asked any more (`question_gone`: answered or dismissed in the session first, another question asked, or its dialog not on the session's screen; for a pick, the session's screen doesn't show its prompt or that option any more; nothing was typed). Readers take a value they don't know as a failure without a reason.

questionAnswer.description: What a session message answers instead of saying something: the question an agent asks in its own dialog (Claude Code's `AskUserQuestion`, GitHub Copilot's `ask_user`, Droid's `AskUser`, OpenCode's `question`, Grok Build's `ask_user_question`, Kimi Code's `AskUserQuestion`), by the tool call that asked it (`call_id`, as the chat's `tool_call` names it), and the answer to each of its questions, in the order asked: the labels of the options chosen (one for a question that takes one) and what's typed as the dialog's own free answer, if anything. Its machine gives it to that dialog, never as typed text, and only while the session shows that chat and its agent asks something; never to a prompt for permission.

question.description: The question as the agent asked it: plain text, tab and LF allowed.

choices.description: The labels of the options chosen, as the agent offered them.

text.description: The free answer: one visible line.

choicePrompt.description: A prompt a session's agent shows on its screen that is answered by picking one of its numbered options (Claude Code's prompts for permission, `Do you want to proceed?`, and its plan to approve), as its machine read it off the screen: its `title` (`Bash command`, `Edit file`, `Ready to code?`), what it's about as far as the screen shows (`detail`: the command, the file's changes, the plan; masked as chat text is), its `question` and the `options` picked as they are (one that opens a field to type in isn't listed), each by the `number` that picks it. `key` names this very prompt: another prompt (another command, question or options) has another, and an answer (`choiceAnswer`) picks an option only while the screen still shows the prompt it names.

detail.description: Plain text of at most 2000 characters: tab and LF allowed.

choiceKey.description: Names a prompt with numbered options as its machine read it off the screen (`choicePrompt`): 16 lowercase hex digits.

choiceNumber.description: An option's number on screen, the key that picks it.

choiceAnswer.description: What a session message picks instead of saying something: option `option` (its `number`) of the prompt `key` the session's agent shows (`sessionState` `choice`). Its machine picks it, one key, only while the session is live, not private, its agent asks something and its screen shows that prompt with that option; never typed as text.

reply.description: What the user wrote back to a feed entry, for its machine to type into the entry's session, and where it is up to; or, without `entry` and `thread`, a session message: what the user wrote to a session itself, which has no answer to reply to yet. The agent's next reply there names it as `reply_to`. A session message with `answer` answers the question its agent asks in its own dialog instead, and one with `choice` picks an option of the prompt its agent shows; no reply names either.

seq.description: The account's order of reply changes: a reply takes a new seq whenever its status changes.

entry.description: The entry replied to; absent on a session message.

thread.description: The entry that started the thread; absent on a session message.

machine.description: The session's machine, which delivers it.

conversation_id.description: The chat a reply answers; on a session message, the chat the session showed when it was written, when it said.

attachments.description: Files the user attached on rakumux.com, in the order attached; absent without any. While the reply is pending, its machine fetches each one from `GET /api/v1/feed/replies/attachments/{id}` (authorized like its other feed requests), saves it and types its path after the text; when one can't be fetched or isn't `size` bytes, it types nothing and reports `attachment_unavailable`. The cloud sends a reply with attachments only to a reader whose machine advertises `reply_attachments` (`sessions-upload` `capabilities`), so older machines never see one. Still listed once the reply stops being pending and its files are gone.

from.description: The machine it was written on; absent when written on rakumux.com.

answer.description: On a session message, in the chat `conversation_id`: the answer to the question its agent asks in its own dialog, given to that dialog in place of typing `text` (which says the answer, for showing). Sent only to a reader that asks with `question_answers=1` and whose machine advertises `question_answers` in its session list, so older machines never see one.

choice.description: On a session message: the option it picks of the prompt its agent shows (`sessionState` `choice`), picked in place of typing `text` (which says the pick, for showing). Sent only to a reader that asks with `choice_answers=1` and whose machine advertises `choice_answers` in its session list, so older machines never see one.

response.description: The entry that answered it, once one did.

entry.description: One feed entry as the cloud returns it.

reply_to.description: The feed reply this turn answers.

thread.description: With `reply_to`: the entry that started the thread (the one first replied to).

prompt.description: What the user asked that started the entry's turn, from its uploaded chat; absent when the chat wasn't uploaded.

turnPrompt.description: The user's message that started a turn, its text cut to 4096 UTF-8 bytes for the feed (`truncated` says so). `id` is the message's id in its chat; an open turn and the entry that finishes it name the same one.

openTurn.description: A prompt still waiting for its answer: a chat's newest user message with no entry finishing at or after it, sent in the last 6 hours.

sessionState.description: One of a machine's sessions as its TUI's Status, Folders and App tabs see it: its name, folder (last path component) and branch, its agent, or without one of those the `program` its App tab files it under (an agent Rakumux doesn't name, else its foreground program while it runs, else the program it started with; never a shell, absent then), whether it runs (`live`) or has ended (`exited`), what its program is doing (`lifecycle`, and the agent's finer `phase` when it reports one), the conversation it shows, whether it's pinned, when it was last used, the places it has worked in (`places`, to a cloud that takes them), its agent's latest step (`output`, to a cloud that takes it), and the prompt with numbered options its agent shows (`choice`, to a cloud that takes it). Private sessions are never listed.

places.description: The places the session has worked in, most recent first: the 8 most recent of those its machine keeps. Sent only to a cloud that said it takes them (`sessions-stored` `accepts` has `places`); absent without any.

output.description: Its agent's latest step as Rakumux's session row shows it: its reasoning, a tool call or its reply, as one line, keys, credential assignments and tokens masked as chat text is, cut to 300 characters. Only for a live session whose agent the feed takes, and only to a cloud that said it takes it (`sessions-stored` `accepts` has `output`); absent otherwise.

choice.description: The prompt with numbered options its agent shows now, for answering from rakumux.com (`choiceAnswer`). Only while the session is live and its agent asks something, only from a machine that advertises `choice_answers`, and only to a cloud that said it takes it (`sessions-stored` `accepts` has `choices`); absent otherwise.

heartbeat.description: The heartbeat this session is a run of. Only to a cloud that said it takes it (`sessions-stored` `accepts` has `heartbeats`); absent otherwise.

sessionPlace.description: A place a session has worked in, as its machine read it from the session's agent's conversation and terminal: a git working tree where it changed files (earlier machines also sent ones it only worked in, `edited` false, and folders outside any repository, without `branch`). `name` is its path in the session's folder when it's there (`inside`; `.` for the folder itself, `worktrees/fix` below it), else its last path component (`rakumux-cloud`): never an absolute path or `..`. `branch` and `worktree` (a linked worktree's name) are its git context when the session last worked there (no `branch` while its HEAD is detached); `edited` says files there were changed; `last_at` is when the session last worked there (the machine's clock, Unix ms).

newSessionStatus.description: `pending` until its machine starts the session (`created`) or can't (`failed`); `expired` when it stayed pending 10 minutes.

newSessionFailure.description: Why a machine didn't start a new session asked for on rakumux.com: it doesn't take new sessions from rakumux.com (`not_accepted`: only from older releases, while a setting of theirs is off), it lists no folder of that name now, or several and `folder_session` doesn't say which (`folder_unknown`), or its daemon couldn't start the session (`refused`). Readers take a value they don't know as a failure without a reason.

createdSession.description: The session a machine started for a new session asked for on rakumux.com: its id and the name its daemon gave it. It appears in the machine's next session list.

newSession.description: A new session asked for on rakumux.com, for one of the account's machines to start in one of the folders its session list names: a login shell in the folder, with `agent` started in it when one is named. It never carries a path or a command: the machine finds the folder among its own by name (`folder_session`, a session rakumux.com listed in that folder, tells two folders of one name apart) and starts the agent as it would itself. `session` is the session it started, once `created`.

id.description: The ULID rakumux.com gave the request: a machine starts at most one session for an id.

machine.description: The machine to start it on, as its session list names it.

folder.description: The folder's last path component, as the machine's session list names it; never a path.

folder_session.description: A session of the machine's that rakumux.com listed in that folder, when it listed one: of the machine's folders with that name, the one this session belongs to.

agent.description: The agent to start in the new session's shell; absent: the shell alone. Other than `claude-code`, `codex` and `opencode`, only for a machine whose latest session list advertises `new_session_agents`.

status_at.description: When its status last changed (`created_at` while pending).

sessionDeletionStatus.description: `pending` until its machine deletes the session (`deleted`) or can't (`failed`); `expired` when it stayed pending 10 minutes.

sessionDeletionFailure.description: Why a machine didn't delete a session asked of it on rakumux.com: it doesn't list that session now (`not_listed`: gone already, or private) or its daemon couldn't delete it (`refused`). Readers take a value they don't know as a failure without a reason.

sessionDeletion.description: A session asked on rakumux.com to be deleted, for the machine that lists it. It names the session by its id, never a path or a command. The machine deletes only a session it lists to rakumux.com, into its session history, and reports it.

id.description: The ULID the page made for the request: a machine carries out at most one deletion for an id.

machine.description: The machine the session is on, as its session list names it.

session.description: The session to delete, by the id the machine's session list gives it.

status_at.description: When its status last changed (`created_at` while pending).

sessionRenameStatus.description: `pending` until its machine renames the session (`renamed`) or can't (`failed`); `expired` when it stayed pending 10 minutes.

sessionRenameFailure.description: Why a machine didn't rename a session asked of it on rakumux.com: it doesn't list that session now (`not_listed`: gone already, or private), another session of its folder has that name (`name_taken`: names are unique within a folder), or its daemon couldn't rename it (`refused`). Readers take a value they don't know as a failure without a reason.

sessionName.description: A session's new name: one visible line of at most 64 characters, without white space at either end.

sessionRename.description: A session asked on rakumux.com to be renamed, for the machine that lists it. It names the session by its id and carries the new name, never a path or a command. The machine renames only a session it lists to rakumux.com, as its user would, and reports it.

id.description: The ULID the page made for the request: a machine carries out at most one rename for an id.

machine.description: The machine the session is on, as its session list names it.

session.description: The session to rename, by the id the machine's session list gives it.

status_at.description: When its status last changed (`created_at` while pending).

heartbeatSchedule.description: When a heartbeat runs, in its machine's local time: every `minutes` (counted from the last due time), daily at `at`, or on the weekdays `days` at `at`. Readers take a `kind` they don't know as no schedule.

heartbeatTime.description: A time of day, `HH:MM` on a 24-hour clock.

heartbeatText.description: A heartbeat's command or task as plain text, masked on the machine as chat text is (keys, credential assignments and tokens; the home directory as `~`). Tab, LF and CR are allowed; other terminal controls, format controls, default-ignorables and lone surrogates are not. May be empty.

heartbeatRunOutcome.description: How a heartbeat's run went: `started` (its session started, its task not typed yet), `task_given` (its agent took the task), `no_agent` (the agent's prompt never showed), `skipped` (an earlier run was still at work at the due time) or `failed` (its session couldn't start). Readers take a value they don't know as unknown.

heartbeatState.description: One of a machine's heartbeats: a task its daemon runs on a clock, each run a new session in its folder. Sent whole by the machine (`heartbeats-upload`), its command and task masked; never a path (its folder's name only).

id.description: The daemon's id for the heartbeat (shown as `hb_` and this).

folder.description: The last path component of the folder its runs start in.

agent.description: The agent its runs start, when it's one the feed names; absent otherwise.

command.description: What its runs start in a login shell (the agent and its flags), masked.

prompt.description: The task typed to the agent once its prompt shows, masked.

schedule.description: Absent when it has none, or one this contract doesn't name.

awaiting_approval.description: An agent made or changed it: paused until the user reads it and approves it (`enable`).

by_agent.description: An agent made it (a session, not the user).

updated_at.description: When it last changed: the version an `enable` action names, so what the user approved is what runs.

next_run_at.description: When it runs next, while it's enabled.

runs.description: How many runs it has started.

session.description: The run's session, by the id the machine's session list gives it.

heartbeatRunRef.description: The heartbeat a session is a run of, and which run.

heartbeatActionStatus.description: `pending` until its machine carries it out (`done`) or can't (`failed`); `expired` when it stayed pending 10 minutes.

heartbeatActionFailure.description: Why a machine didn't carry out a heartbeat action asked of it on rakumux.com: it has no such heartbeat now (`not_listed`), the heartbeat changed since the version approved (`changed`: read it again), it has no command, task or schedule to run with (`incomplete`), or its daemon refused (`refused`). Readers take a value they don't know as a failure without a reason.

heartbeatAction.description: Something asked on rakumux.com of one of a machine's heartbeats: `enable` (approve it, when an agent made or changed it, and turn it on), `pause` or `run` (a run now). It names the heartbeat by its id, never a path, a command or a task. The machine carries it out as its user would and reports it.

id.description: The ULID the page made for the request: a machine carries out at most one action for an id.

machine.description: The machine the heartbeat is on, as its session list names it.

heartbeat.description: The heartbeat, by the id the machine's heartbeats upload gives it.

updated_at.description: For `enable`: the heartbeat's `updated_at` the user saw as they approved it. The machine enables it only while it's still that version.

session.description: With `done` for `run`: the run's session, by the id the machine's session list gives it.

status_at.description: When its status last changed (`created_at` while pending).

rakumuxVersion.description: A stable Rakumux release's version, as its tag names it without the `v` (`0.1.48`).

release.description: The newest stable Rakumux release rakumux.com knows of: GitHub's latest release of `humanunsupervised/rakumux`, read every few minutes and as soon as one is published. A machine's account service passes it to the TUIs, which offer the update.

machineUpdate.description: An update to `version` asked of a machine on rakumux.com, as the replies read brings it to that machine (only to one whose session list says `remote_update`): the machine installs that release through its verified update path, restarts its server in place (its sessions keep running) and its services, and reports how that went (`update-status`).

id.description: The ULID rakumux.com gave the request: a machine installs at most once for an id.

machineUpdateState.description: An update asked of a machine on rakumux.com, as rakumux.com keeps it: the release, where it is, and why it failed.

status_at.description: When its status last changed (`created_at` while pending).

machineUpdateStatus.description: Where an update asked of a machine is: waiting for the machine to read it (`pending`), being installed (`installing`), installed with the server and its services restarted in place (`updated`), not done (`failed`, with why), or not reported done within 15 minutes (`expired`).

machineUpdateFailure.description: Why a machine didn't update: its installation can't update itself (`unsupported`: npm, Homebrew or a source build, updated there by hand), the release couldn't be installed (`install_failed`: a download, signature or checksum failure, an installation it can't write), or it was installed but the server couldn't restart in place (`restart_failed`: the new version runs once Rakumux restarts). Readers take a value they don't know as a failure without a reason.
